errors.text_span: This diagram illustrates the relationship between sampling time and accuracy for various methods, comparing their performance. The x-axis represents sampling time, ranging from 0 to 70 in increments of 10, while the y-axis represents accuracy, spanning from 60 to 88 in increments of 4. The diagram includes six distinct lines, each representing a different method: DiP (purple, solid line, triangle markers), AnP (orange, solid line, triangle markers), CoT (blue, solid line, triangle markers), L2M (cyan, solid line, triangle markers), Dynamic w/ Oracle (black, dashed line, square markers), and Adaptive + Dynamic w/ Oracle (red, dashed line, circle markers). DiP starts at approximately (0, 60) and increases to around (30, 78), remaining relatively stable thereafter, reaching (70, 78). AnP begins at about (0, 66) and rises to roughly (10, 74), then gradually increases to (70, 75). CoT starts at (0, 60) and jumps to around (10, 74), continuing to rise to (30, 78) before stabilizing at (70, 79). L2M begins at (0, 60) and surges to approximately (10, 72), further increasing to (30, 78) and eventually reaching (70, 80). Dynamic w/ Oracle remains relatively constant around 84 across the sampling time range, starting at (0, 84) and ending at (70, 85). Adaptive + Dynamic w/ Oracle starts at approximately (0, 86) and increases to around (10, 88), remaining stable at (70, 89). SBP is also plotted (peach, solid line, triangle markers), starting at approximately (0, 68), rising to around (10, 75), and stabilizing near (70, 76).
